recommendations.name: Diesel genset displacement with solar plus storage
recommendations.description: Reduce genset running hours by combining rooftop PV with a modest battery to ride through short outages.
recommendations.why: Diesel is the most expensive electricity in the plant. Displacing it is usually profitable before carbon is even counted.
recommendations.evidence: Comparative LCOE of diesel genset versus solar plus storage in India
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 23,100 litres of diesel a year.

recommendations.name: Idle load elimination and production scheduling
recommendations.description: Shut compressors, exhaust fans, chillers and ovens during breaks and changeovers; consolidate short batches to cut furnace and boiler warm-up cycles.
recommendations.why: Almost free, but it is a behaviour change and it decays without metering and a named owner.
recommendations.evidence: Energy management system case studies under ISO 50001
caveats: Savings regress within 6-9 months unless sub-metering makes the loss visible to the shift supervisor
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 150,000 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Compressed air leak survey and repair
recommendations.description: Ultrasonic leak detection across the compressed air ring main, followed by tagged repair. Typical industrial systems lose 20-30 percent of compressor output to leaks; compressed air is commonly 10-15 percent of plant electricity.
recommendations.why: The cheapest tonne of carbon in almost every factory. Pays back in weeks and needs no production stoppage.
recommendations.evidence: BEE SME sector energy audit findings; widely replicated across Indian industrial clusters
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 120,000 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: LED lighting retrofit
recommendations.description: Replace fluorescent, metal halide and sodium fixtures with LED across shopfloor and yard.
recommendations.why: Low risk, self-funding, and it also cuts lamp replacement labour.
recommendations.evidence: EESL bulk procurement programme outcomes
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 90,000 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Recycled cotton yarn blending
recommendations.description: Blend mechanically recycled cotton into yarn for the product lines where hand feel and strength permit.
recommendations.why: Cotton dominates a textile SME footprint far more than its energy bill does, so this outranks most energy projects on tonnes.
recommendations.evidence: Textile Exchange recycled cotton LCA
caveats: Staple length loss caps blend ratio, commonly at 20-30 percent
Export buyers increasingly require certified recycled content, which adds audit cost but also price premium
recommendations.physical_note: Switches about 662 tonnes a year from Conventional cotton yarn (5.5 tCO2e/t) to Recycled cotton yarn (1.8 tCO2e/t), a saving of 3.7 tCO2e per tonne switched. Capped at 25 percent of the material stream by specification limits.

recommendations.name: Variable frequency drives on pumps and fans
recommendations.description: Fit VFDs to centrifugal pumps, fans and blowers currently running at fixed speed with throttled flow. Affinity laws mean a 20 percent speed cut is roughly a 50 percent power cut.
recommendations.why: Largest reliable electrical saving available to most process plants without changing the process itself.
recommendations.evidence: BEE PAT scheme documented motor system savings
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 240,000 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Power factor correction and capacitor bank
recommendations.description: Automatic power factor control to lift PF above the utility threshold, removing penalty and releasing transformer capacity.
recommendations.why: Mostly a tariff play rather than a carbon play. The engine ranks it on cash, and is explicit that its carbon benefit is small.
recommendations.evidence: State DISCOM tariff penalty structures
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 30,000 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Premium efficiency motor replacement
recommendations.description: Replace IE1/IE2 motors above 7.5 kW with IE4 or IE5 units at end of life or on failure.
recommendations.why: Best done on failure rather than as a forced swap; the engine flags it as opportunistic.
recommendations.evidence: IEC 60034-30-1 efficiency class deltas
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 105,000 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Captive rooftop solar PV
recommendations.description: Behind-the-meter rooftop PV sized to daytime base load. Indian specific yield is typically 1400-1500 kWh per kWp per year.
recommendations.why: The headline move for most SMEs. Ceiling is set by roof area and daytime load coincidence, not by willingness.
recommendations.evidence: MNRE rooftop programme benchmark costs; typical 3.5-5 year payback at industrial tariffs
caveats: Requires shadow-free roof area of roughly 8-10 sq m per kWp
Net metering rules and capacity caps vary by state DISCOM
Benefit collapses if the plant runs mainly on night shift
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 750,000 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Substitute rPET for virgin PET
recommendations.description: Move to food-grade or industrial-grade recycled PET for the share of output where regulation and specification permit.
recommendations.why: Also front-runs EPR obligations under the Plastic Waste Management Rules, which mandate recycled content targets.
recommendations.evidence: Plastic Waste Management Rules recycled content schedule
caveats: Food contact applications require specific grade approval
Colour and clarity constraints limit substitutable share
recommendations.physical_note: Switches about 90 tonnes a year from Virgin PET resin (3 tCO2e/t) to rPET (mechanical) (1.3 tCO2e/t), a saving of 1.7 tCO2e per tonne switched. Capped at 50 percent of the material stream by specification limits.

recommendations.name: Steam line and furnace insulation upgrade
recommendations.description: Re-lag bare or degraded steam and hot fluid lines, valves and flanges; repair furnace door and wall refractory.
recommendations.why: Cheap, fast, and it also fixes a real shopfloor burn hazard.
recommendations.evidence: Standard insulation heat loss calculations
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 2,480 GJ a year of process heat, roughly 156 tonnes of coal equivalent.

recommendations.name: Steam trap survey and condensate recovery
recommendations.description: Survey and replace failed steam traps, and return hot condensate to the boiler feed tank instead of dumping it to drain.
recommendations.why: A genuine closed loop: the heat and the treated water both come back. Usually under an 18 month payback.
recommendations.evidence: BEE boiler system audit norms
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 3,721 GJ a year of process heat, roughly 234 tonnes of coal equivalent.

recommendations.name: Shift bulk inbound freight from road to rail
recommendations.description: Move bulk raw material inbound legs above roughly 500 km from road to rail where a siding or terminal is reachable.
recommendations.why: Rail is roughly four times better per tonne-km and usually cheaper on long bulk hauls. The blocker is lead time, not cost.
recommendations.evidence: Comparative modal emission factors; Dedicated Freight Corridor capacity
caveats: Longer and less predictable transit forces higher safety stock
Needs first and last mile road legs, which claw back part of the saving
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 585,000 tonne-km of freight a year.

recommendations.name: Waste heat recovery on flue gas
recommendations.description: Economiser or recuperator on boiler or furnace exhaust to preheat feedwater or combustion air.
recommendations.why: Recovers energy the plant has already paid for and is currently sending up the stack.
recommendations.evidence: BEE PAT scheme waste heat recovery case studies
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 6,201 GJ a year of process heat, roughly 390 tonnes of coal equivalent.

recommendations.name: Solar thermal process water preheating
recommendations.description: Evacuated tube or concentrating collectors to preheat process water below 90 degrees C, cutting boiler duty.
recommendations.why: Only works for genuinely low temperature duty, which is exactly where dyeing and food plants waste the most fuel.
recommendations.evidence: MNRE solar thermal programme
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 7,441 GJ a year of process heat, roughly 468 tonnes of coal equivalent.

recommendations.name: Source segregation and recycling contract
recommendations.description: Segregate at source into dry recyclable, organic and hazardous streams, and contract an authorised recycler instead of mixed landfill disposal.
recommendations.why: Usually cash positive because segregated dry recyclables have resale value while mixed waste carries a disposal charge.
recommendations.evidence: Solid Waste Management Rules; CPCB authorised recycler framework

recommendations.name: Renewable power via open access or green tariff
recommendations.description: Contract renewable electricity through open access, a group captive arrangement, or the DISCOM green tariff.
recommendations.why: Near-zero capex route to a large Scope 2 cut. You still buy the electricity, so the cash case is only the tariff differential - typically a small saving, and negative in states with heavy cross-subsidy surcharge. The carbon case is the reason to do it.
recommendations.evidence: State open access regulations; group captive structures under Electricity Rules
caveats: Open access is often only economic above roughly 1 MW contracted demand
Cross-subsidy surcharge and additional surcharge can erase the tariff saving
Requires a genuine RE attribute claim to be Scope 2 market-method compliant
recommendations.physical_note: Re-sources about 1,500,000 kWh a year to renewable supply. The plant still buys this power, so the cash effect is only the tariff differential of Rs 0.35/kWh.

recommendations.name: Supplier radius reduction
recommendations.description: Requalify high-volume, low-value inputs to suppliers within a shorter radius, cutting inbound tonne-km.
recommendations.why: Real but slow, and it competes with unit price. The engine ranks it low unless freight is a large share of the footprint.
recommendations.evidence: Supply chain footprint studies
caveats: Local supply often costs more per unit, which can outweigh the freight saving
Evidence base in Indian SME contexts is thin, hence low confidence
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 390,000 tonne-km of freight a year.

recommendations.name: Fuel switch to agri-residue briquette
recommendations.description: Convert or replace a coal or furnace oil boiler to fire agri-residue briquettes. Biogenic CO2 is reported separately from the Scope 1 total under GHG Protocol.
recommendations.why: The single largest Scope 1 cut available to a thermal-heavy SME, and it turns a regional waste stream into a fuel. On current prices briquettes cost MORE per GJ than coal, so this is a genuine net cost - it is the plant's biggest decarbonisation lever and it is not free.
recommendations.evidence: Widely deployed in Tamil Nadu and Punjab industrial clusters
caveats: Briquette supply and price are seasonal and regionally volatile
Higher ash handling and more frequent cleaning than furnace oil
Boiler warranty and insurance implications must be checked before conversion
Biogenic carbon must be disclosed separately, not netted silently
recommendations.physical_note: Replaces about 52,708 GJ a year of current fuel with Agri-residue briquette. Current delivered cost is Rs 409/GJ against Rs 480/GJ for the replacement, so the fuel bill costs an extra Rs 37.5 lakh a year.

recommendations.name: Outbound load consolidation and route planning
recommendations.description: Consolidate part loads, raise fill factor and plan multi-drop routes rather than despatching on demand.
recommendations.why: Pure logistics discipline. Cuts freight spend and emissions in the same proportion.
recommendations.evidence: Standard freight fill factor improvement practice
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 292,500 tonne-km of freight a year.

recommendations.name: Dye bath reuse and closed loop water recovery
recommendations.description: Reuse of exhausted dye bath liquor plus RO recovery of treated effluent, cutting both fresh water heating duty and effluent load.
recommendations.why: Every litre not freshly heated is fuel not burned. In Tirupur this is already a regulatory expectation, not an option.
recommendations.evidence: Tirupur zero liquid discharge cluster experience
caveats: ZLD systems carry high electrical load, which partly offsets the thermal saving
Salt build-up limits the number of reuse cycles
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 11,162 GJ a year of process heat, roughly 702 tonnes of coal equivalent.

assumptions.derating_note: Portfolio totals apply each intervention to the RESIDUAL stream in cost order, not to the original baseline. Standalone and de-rated abatement are both shown on every card. assumptions.capex_note: Screening-grade intervention library. Every economic figure is an order-of-magnitude planning estimate intended to rank options, not to replace a vendor quotation. The UI states this on every card.

cbam.applicability: Sector 'Textile dyeing, bleaching and processing' is exempt from CBAM Phase 1 (2026). Current statutory border liability is ₹0. Under active European Commission Article 30 review for post-2027 extension.
cbam.basis: Sector is outside EU CBAM Regulation (EU) 2023/956 Annex I scope in Phase 1 (2026 definitive regime).
cbam.caveat: Indicative screening only. CBAM surrender liability requires installation-level verified data and customs CN code mapping. Final certificate price depends on weekly EU ETS auctions.

SEBI BRSR Core requires reasonable assurance on primary source documents. Working papers prepared; external assurance requires primary evidence in Evidence Vault.

methodology.factor_note: Every factor carries a source and an uncertainty band. The engine propagates the band to every result. Point estimates are never shown without their range.
methodology.verification_status: HACKATHON BUILD - factors are literature values and must be re-verified against the primary source editions cited before commercial use.
methodology.benchmark_note: Benchmarks are indicative screening percentiles compiled for this build from published sector energy-intensity literature and cluster study ranges. They are good enough to rank a plant against its peers and to flag outliers, and are NOT a substitute for a BEE-accredited audit. Replace with cluster-specific survey data before production use.
methodology.leak_rule: A stream is flagged as a LEAK POINT when its intensity exceeds the sector p75, or when it contributes more than 15 percent of total footprint AND sits above p50. Severity scales with the distance above p75.

recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 4,200,000 tonne-km of freight a year.

recommendations.name: Idle load elimination and production scheduling
recommendations.description: Shut compressors, exhaust fans, chillers and ovens during breaks and changeovers; consolidate short batches to cut furnace and boiler warm-up cycles.
recommendations.why: Almost free, but it is a behaviour change and it decays without metering and a named owner.
recommendations.evidence: Energy management system case studies under ISO 50001
caveats: Savings regress within 6-9 months unless sub-metering makes the loss visible to the shift supervisor
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 126,000 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Compressed air leak survey and repair
recommendations.description: Ultrasonic leak detection across the compressed air ring main, followed by tagged repair. Typical industrial systems lose 20-30 percent of compressor output to leaks; compressed air is commonly 10-15 percent of plant electricity.
recommendations.why: The cheapest tonne of carbon in almost every factory. Pays back in weeks and needs no production stoppage.
recommendations.evidence: BEE SME sector energy audit findings; widely replicated across Indian industrial clusters
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 100,800 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: LED lighting retrofit
recommendations.description: Replace fluorescent, metal halide and sodium fixtures with LED across shopfloor and yard.
recommendations.why: Low risk, self-funding, and it also cuts lamp replacement labour.
recommendations.evidence: EESL bulk procurement programme outcomes
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 75,600 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Variable frequency drives on pumps and fans
recommendations.description: Fit VFDs to centrifugal pumps, fans and blowers currently running at fixed speed with throttled flow. Affinity laws mean a 20 percent speed cut is roughly a 50 percent power cut.
recommendations.why: Largest reliable electrical saving available to most process plants without changing the process itself.
recommendations.evidence: BEE PAT scheme documented motor system savings
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 201,600 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Premium efficiency motor replacement
recommendations.description: Replace IE1/IE2 motors above 7.5 kW with IE4 or IE5 units at end of life or on failure.
recommendations.why: Best done on failure rather than as a forced swap; the engine flags it as opportunistic.
recommendations.evidence: IEC 60034-30-1 efficiency class deltas
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 88,200 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Captive rooftop solar PV
recommendations.description: Behind-the-meter rooftop PV sized to daytime base load. Indian specific yield is typically 1400-1500 kWh per kWp per year.

Benefit collapses if the plant runs mainly on night shift
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 630,000 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Power factor correction and capacitor bank

recommendations.why: Mostly a tariff play rather than a carbon play. The engine ranks it on cash, and is explicit that its carbon benefit is small.

recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 25,200 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Source segregation and recycling contract

recommendations.evidence: Solid Waste Management Rules; CPCB authorised recycler framework

recommendations.name: Increase scrap charge in steel input
recommendations.description: Shift procurement toward secondary steel produced via scrap-based induction or electric arc furnace routes.
recommendations.why: Roughly a 75 percent embodied carbon reduction per tonne switched, with a modest price advantage.
recommendations.evidence: worldsteel life cycle inventory, scrap versus BF-BOF route
recommendations.physical_note: Switches about 1,102 tonnes a year from Primary steel (BF-BOF route) (2.2 tCO2e/t) to Secondary steel (scrap, EAF/induction) (0.55 tCO2e/t), a saving of 1.65 tCO2e per tonne switched. Capped at 80 percent of the material stream by specification limits.

recommendations.name: Switch to recycled aluminium feedstock
recommendations.description: Substitute primary aluminium ingot with verified secondary or recycled ingot for grades where specification allows.
recommendations.why: Recycled aluminium carries roughly 95 percent less embodied carbon than primary and usually costs less per tonne. It is the highest-leverage circular move in the whole library.
recommendations.evidence: International Aluminium Institute recycling LCI
caveats: Alloy specification and trace element limits cap the substitutable fraction
Requires qualified supplier with consistent composition certification
Customer drawing approval may be needed for structural parts
recommendations.physical_note: Switches about 195 tonnes a year from Primary aluminium (13 tCO2e/t) to Recycled aluminium (0.6 tCO2e/t), a saving of 12.4 tCO2e per tonne switched.

recommendations.name: Shift bulk inbound freight from road to rail
recommendations.description: Move bulk raw material inbound legs above roughly 500 km from road to rail where a siding or terminal is reachable.
recommendations.why: Rail is roughly four times better per tonne-km and usually cheaper on long bulk hauls. The blocker is lead time, not cost.
recommendations.evidence: Comparative modal emission factors; Dedicated Freight Corridor capacity
caveats: Longer and less predictable transit forces higher safety stock
Needs first and last mile road legs, which claw back part of the saving
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 870,000 tonne-km of freight a year.

recommendations.name: Renewable power via open access or green tariff
recommendations.description: Contract renewable electricity through open access, a group captive arrangement, or the DISCOM green tariff.
recommendations.why: Near-zero capex route to a large Scope 2 cut. You still buy the electricity, so the cash case is only the tariff differential - typically a small saving, and negative in states with heavy cross-subsidy surcharge. The carbon case is the reason to do it.
recommendations.evidence: State open access regulations; group captive structures under Electricity Rules
caveats: Open access is often only economic above roughly 1 MW contracted demand
Cross-subsidy surcharge and additional surcharge can erase the tariff saving
Requires a genuine RE attribute claim to be Scope 2 market-method compliant
recommendations.physical_note: Re-sources about 1,260,000 kWh a year to renewable supply. The plant still buys this power, so the cash effect is only the tariff differential of Rs 0.35/kWh.

recommendations.name: In-house process scrap recovery and re-melt
recommendations.description: Segregate runners, sprues, trim and rejects by grade at the machine, and reintroduce them as feedstock instead of selling as mixed scrap.
recommendations.why: The tightest possible loop, entirely inside the factory gate, with no supplier qualification needed.
recommendations.evidence: Standard plastics and foundry yield improvement practice
caveats: Contamination control is the whole game; mixed-grade regrind destroys the benefit
Regrind ratio is capped by part quality requirements

recommendations.name: Supplier radius reduction
recommendations.description: Requalify high-volume, low-value inputs to suppliers within a shorter radius, cutting inbound tonne-km.
recommendations.why: Real but slow, and it competes with unit price. The engine ranks it low unless freight is a large share of the footprint.
recommendations.evidence: Supply chain footprint studies
caveats: Local supply often costs more per unit, which can outweigh the freight saving
Evidence base in Indian SME contexts is thin, hence low confidence
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 580,000 tonne-km of freight a year.

recommendations.name: Outbound load consolidation and route planning
recommendations.description: Consolidate part loads, raise fill factor and plan multi-drop routes rather than despatching on demand.
recommendations.why: Pure logistics discipline. Cuts freight spend and emissions in the same proportion.
recommendations.evidence: Standard freight fill factor improvement practice
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 435,000 tonne-km of freight a year.

recommendations.name: Source segregation and recycling contract
recommendations.description: Segregate at source into dry recyclable, organic and hazardous streams, and contract an authorised recycler instead of mixed landfill disposal.
recommendations.why: Usually cash positive because segregated dry recyclables have resale value while mixed waste carries a disposal charge.
recommendations.evidence: Solid Waste Management Rules; CPCB authorised recycler framework

recommendations.name: Diesel genset displacement with solar plus storage
recommendations.description: Reduce genset running hours by combining rooftop PV with a modest battery to ride through short outages.
recommendations.why: Diesel is the most expensive electricity in the plant. Displacing it is usually profitable before carbon is even counted.
recommendations.evidence: Comparative LCOE of diesel genset versus solar plus storage in India
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 14,300 litres of diesel a year.

recommendations.name: Idle load elimination and production scheduling
recommendations.description: Shut compressors, exhaust fans, chillers and ovens during breaks and changeovers; consolidate short batches to cut furnace and boiler warm-up cycles.
recommendations.why: Almost free, but it is a behaviour change and it decays without metering and a named owner.
recommendations.evidence: Energy management system case studies under ISO 50001
caveats: Savings regress within 6-9 months unless sub-metering makes the loss visible to the shift supervisor
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 120,250 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Compressed air leak survey and repair
recommendations.description: Ultrasonic leak detection across the compressed air ring main, followed by tagged repair. Typical industrial systems lose 20-30 percent of compressor output to leaks; compressed air is commonly 10-15 percent of plant electricity.
recommendations.why: The cheapest tonne of carbon in almost every factory. Pays back in weeks and needs no production stoppage.
recommendations.evidence: BEE SME sector energy audit findings; widely replicated across Indian industrial clusters
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 96,200 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: LED lighting retrofit
recommendations.description: Replace fluorescent, metal halide and sodium fixtures with LED across shopfloor and yard.
recommendations.why: Low risk, self-funding, and it also cuts lamp replacement labour.
recommendations.evidence: EESL bulk procurement programme outcomes
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 72,150 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Recycled content corrugate and packaging
recommendations.description: Specify recycled content board for secondary and transit packaging, and right-size box dimensions to cut material per despatch.
recommendations.why: Nearly frictionless. Recycled board is cheaper and the substitution rarely needs customer sign-off for transit packaging.
recommendations.evidence: CEPI recycled grade material factors
recommendations.physical_note: Switches about 144 tonnes a year from Virgin kraft / corrugate (1.25 tCO2e/t) to Recycled content board (0.8 tCO2e/t), a saving of 0.45 tCO2e per tonne switched. Capped at 90 percent of the material stream by specification limits.

recommendations.name: Variable frequency drives on pumps and fans
recommendations.description: Fit VFDs to centrifugal pumps, fans and blowers currently running at fixed speed with throttled flow. Affinity laws mean a 20 percent speed cut is roughly a 50 percent power cut.
recommendations.why: Largest reliable electrical saving available to most process plants without changing the process itself.
recommendations.evidence: BEE PAT scheme documented motor system savings
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 192,400 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Power factor correction and capacitor bank
recommendations.description: Automatic power factor control to lift PF above the utility threshold, removing penalty and releasing transformer capacity.
recommendations.why: Mostly a tariff play rather than a carbon play. The engine ranks it on cash, and is explicit that its carbon benefit is small.
recommendations.evidence: State DISCOM tariff penalty structures
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 24,050 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Premium efficiency motor replacement
recommendations.description: Replace IE1/IE2 motors above 7.5 kW with IE4 or IE5 units at end of life or on failure.
recommendations.why: Best done on failure rather than as a forced swap; the engine flags it as opportunistic.
recommendations.evidence: IEC 60034-30-1 efficiency class deltas
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 84,175 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Captive rooftop solar PV
recommendations.description: Behind-the-meter rooftop PV sized to daytime base load. Indian specific yield is typically 1400-1500 kWh per kWp per year.
recommendations.why: The headline move for most SMEs. Ceiling is set by roof area and daytime load coincidence, not by willingness.
recommendations.evidence: MNRE rooftop programme benchmark costs; typical 3.5-5 year payback at industrial tariffs
caveats: Requires shadow-free roof area of roughly 8-10 sq m per kWp
Net metering rules and capacity caps vary by state DISCOM
Benefit collapses if the plant runs mainly on night shift
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 601,250 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Substitute rPET for virgin PET
recommendations.description: Move to food-grade or industrial-grade recycled PET for the share of output where regulation and specification permit.
recommendations.why: Also front-runs EPR obligations under the Plastic Waste Management Rules, which mandate recycled content targets.
recommendations.evidence: Plastic Waste Management Rules recycled content schedule
caveats: Food contact applications require specific grade approval
Colour and clarity constraints limit substitutable share
recommendations.physical_note: Switches about 990 tonnes a year from Virgin PET resin (3 tCO2e/t) to rPET (mechanical) (1.3 tCO2e/t), a saving of 1.7 tCO2e per tonne switched. Capped at 50 percent of the material stream by specification limits.

recommendations.name: Shift bulk inbound freight from road to rail
recommendations.description: Move bulk raw material inbound legs above roughly 500 km from road to rail where a siding or terminal is reachable.
recommendations.why: Rail is roughly four times better per tonne-km and usually cheaper on long bulk hauls. The blocker is lead time, not cost.
recommendations.evidence: Comparative modal emission factors; Dedicated Freight Corridor capacity
caveats: Longer and less predictable transit forces higher safety stock
Needs first and last mile road legs, which claw back part of the saving
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 495,000 tonne-km of freight a year.

recommendations.name: Renewable power via open access or green tariff
recommendations.description: Contract renewable electricity through open access, a group captive arrangement, or the DISCOM green tariff.
recommendations.why: Near-zero capex route to a large Scope 2 cut. You still buy the electricity, so the cash case is only the tariff differential - typically a small saving, and negative in states with heavy cross-subsidy surcharge. The carbon case is the reason to do it.
recommendations.evidence: State open access regulations; group captive structures under Electricity Rules
caveats: Open access is often only economic above roughly 1 MW contracted demand
Cross-subsidy surcharge and additional surcharge can erase the tariff saving
Requires a genuine RE attribute claim to be Scope 2 market-method compliant
recommendations.physical_note: Re-sources about 1,202,500 kWh a year to renewable supply. The plant still buys this power, so the cash effect is only the tariff differential of Rs 0.35/kWh.

recommendations.name: In-house process scrap recovery and re-melt
recommendations.description: Segregate runners, sprues, trim and rejects by grade at the machine, and reintroduce them as feedstock instead of selling as mixed scrap.
recommendations.why: The tightest possible loop, entirely inside the factory gate, with no supplier qualification needed.
recommendations.evidence: Standard plastics and foundry yield improvement practice
caveats: Contamination control is the whole game; mixed-grade regrind destroys the benefit
Regrind ratio is capped by part quality requirements

recommendations.name: Supplier radius reduction
recommendations.description: Requalify high-volume, low-value inputs to suppliers within a shorter radius, cutting inbound tonne-km.
recommendations.why: Real but slow, and it competes with unit price. The engine ranks it low unless freight is a large share of the footprint.
recommendations.evidence: Supply chain footprint studies
caveats: Local supply often costs more per unit, which can outweigh the freight saving
Evidence base in Indian SME contexts is thin, hence low confidence
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 330,000 tonne-km of freight a year.

recommendations.name: Outbound load consolidation and route planning
recommendations.description: Consolidate part loads, raise fill factor and plan multi-drop routes rather than despatching on demand.
recommendations.why: Pure logistics discipline. Cuts freight spend and emissions in the same proportion.
recommendations.evidence: Standard freight fill factor improvement practice
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 247,500 tonne-km of freight a year.

recommendations.name: Source segregation and recycling contract
recommendations.description: Segregate at source into dry recyclable, organic and hazardous streams, and contract an authorised recycler instead of mixed landfill disposal.
recommendations.why: Usually cash positive because segregated dry recyclables have resale value while mixed waste carries a disposal charge.
recommendations.evidence: Solid Waste Management Rules; CPCB authorised recycler framework

recommendations.name: Diesel genset displacement with solar plus storage
recommendations.description: Reduce genset running hours by combining rooftop PV with a modest battery to ride through short outages.
recommendations.why: Diesel is the most expensive electricity in the plant. Displacing it is usually profitable before carbon is even counted.
recommendations.evidence: Comparative LCOE of diesel genset versus solar plus storage in India
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 24,200 litres of diesel a year.

recommendations.name: Idle load elimination and production scheduling
recommendations.description: Shut compressors, exhaust fans, chillers and ovens during breaks and changeovers; consolidate short batches to cut furnace and boiler warm-up cycles.
recommendations.why: Almost free, but it is a behaviour change and it decays without metering and a named owner.
recommendations.evidence: Energy management system case studies under ISO 50001
caveats: Savings regress within 6-9 months unless sub-metering makes the loss visible to the shift supervisor
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 51,200 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Compressed air leak survey and repair
recommendations.description: Ultrasonic leak detection across the compressed air ring main, followed by tagged repair. Typical industrial systems lose 20-30 percent of compressor output to leaks; compressed air is commonly 10-15 percent of plant electricity.
recommendations.why: The cheapest tonne of carbon in almost every factory. Pays back in weeks and needs no production stoppage.
recommendations.evidence: BEE SME sector energy audit findings; widely replicated across Indian industrial clusters
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 40,960 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: LED lighting retrofit
recommendations.description: Replace fluorescent, metal halide and sodium fixtures with LED across shopfloor and yard.
recommendations.why: Low risk, self-funding, and it also cuts lamp replacement labour.
recommendations.evidence: EESL bulk procurement programme outcomes
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 30,720 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Recycled content corrugate and packaging
recommendations.description: Specify recycled content board for secondary and transit packaging, and right-size box dimensions to cut material per despatch.
recommendations.why: Nearly frictionless. Recycled board is cheaper and the substitution rarely needs customer sign-off for transit packaging.
recommendations.evidence: CEPI recycled grade material factors
recommendations.physical_note: Switches about 81 tonnes a year from Virgin kraft / corrugate (1.25 tCO2e/t) to Recycled content board (0.8 tCO2e/t), a saving of 0.45 tCO2e per tonne switched. Capped at 90 percent of the material stream by specification limits.

recommendations.name: Variable frequency drives on pumps and fans
recommendations.description: Fit VFDs to centrifugal pumps, fans and blowers currently running at fixed speed with throttled flow. Affinity laws mean a 20 percent speed cut is roughly a 50 percent power cut.
recommendations.why: Largest reliable electrical saving available to most process plants without changing the process itself.
recommendations.evidence: BEE PAT scheme documented motor system savings
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 81,920 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Premium efficiency motor replacement
recommendations.description: Replace IE1/IE2 motors above 7.5 kW with IE4 or IE5 units at end of life or on failure.
recommendations.why: Best done on failure rather than as a forced swap; the engine flags it as opportunistic.
recommendations.evidence: IEC 60034-30-1 efficiency class deltas
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 35,840 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Captive rooftop solar PV
recommendations.description: Behind-the-meter rooftop PV sized to daytime base load. Indian specific yield is typically 1400-1500 kWh per kWp per year.
recommendations.why: The headline move for most SMEs. Ceiling is set by roof area and daytime load coincidence, not by willingness.
recommendations.evidence: MNRE rooftop programme benchmark costs; typical 3.5-5 year payback at industrial tariffs
caveats: Requires shadow-free roof area of roughly 8-10 sq m per kWp
Net metering rules and capacity caps vary by state DISCOM
Benefit collapses if the plant runs mainly on night shift
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 256,000 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Increase scrap charge in steel input
recommendations.description: Shift procurement toward secondary steel produced via scrap-based induction or electric arc furnace routes.
recommendations.why: Roughly a 75 percent embodied carbon reduction per tonne switched, with a modest price advantage.
recommendations.evidence: worldsteel life cycle inventory, scrap versus BF-BOF route
recommendations.physical_note: Switches about 1,187 tonnes a year from Primary steel (BF-BOF route) (2.2 tCO2e/t) to Secondary steel (scrap, EAF/induction) (0.55 tCO2e/t), a saving of 1.65 tCO2e per tonne switched.

recommendations.name: Shift bulk inbound freight from road to rail
recommendations.description: Move bulk raw material inbound legs above roughly 500 km from road to rail where a siding or terminal is reachable.
recommendations.why: Rail is roughly four times better per tonne-km and usually cheaper on long bulk hauls. The blocker is lead time, not cost.
recommendations.evidence: Comparative modal emission factors; Dedicated Freight Corridor capacity
caveats: Longer and less predictable transit forces higher safety stock
Needs first and last mile road legs, which claw back part of the saving
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 630,000 tonne-km of freight a year.

recommendations.name: Power factor correction and capacitor bank
recommendations.description: Automatic power factor control to lift PF above the utility threshold, removing penalty and releasing transformer capacity.
recommendations.why: Mostly a tariff play rather than a carbon play. The engine ranks it on cash, and is explicit that its carbon benefit is small.
recommendations.evidence: State DISCOM tariff penalty structures
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 10,240 kWh a year of purchased electricity.

recommendations.name: Renewable power via open access or green tariff
recommendations.description: Contract renewable electricity through open access, a group captive arrangement, or the DISCOM green tariff.
recommendations.why: Near-zero capex route to a large Scope 2 cut. You still buy the electricity, so the cash case is only the tariff differential - typically a small saving, and negative in states with heavy cross-subsidy surcharge. The carbon case is the reason to do it.
recommendations.evidence: State open access regulations; group captive structures under Electricity Rules
caveats: Open access is often only economic above roughly 1 MW contracted demand
Cross-subsidy surcharge and additional surcharge can erase the tariff saving
Requires a genuine RE attribute claim to be Scope 2 market-method compliant
recommendations.physical_note: Re-sources about 512,000 kWh a year to renewable supply. The plant still buys this power, so the cash effect is only the tariff differential of Rs 0.35/kWh.

recommendations.name: Supplier radius reduction
recommendations.description: Requalify high-volume, low-value inputs to suppliers within a shorter radius, cutting inbound tonne-km.
recommendations.why: Real but slow, and it competes with unit price. The engine ranks it low unless freight is a large share of the footprint.
recommendations.evidence: Supply chain footprint studies
caveats: Local supply often costs more per unit, which can outweigh the freight saving
Evidence base in Indian SME contexts is thin, hence low confidence
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 420,000 tonne-km of freight a year.

recommendations.name: Outbound load consolidation and route planning
recommendations.description: Consolidate part loads, raise fill factor and plan multi-drop routes rather than despatching on demand.
recommendations.why: Pure logistics discipline. Cuts freight spend and emissions in the same proportion.
recommendations.evidence: Standard freight fill factor improvement practice
recommendations.physical_note: Avoids about 315,000 tonne-km of freight a year.
